main_text.p: nus est sanguineus, intern[?]ꝰ ferrugineus, duritie tanta ut vix limam sentiat: Hic sanguinem sistere dicitur.
Magnes*Magnes seu siderites est lapis, colore ad cœruleum vergente præditus, ferrum naturali facultate attrahens. Arist,lib.7. Phys. Scal. exerc. 131.

Lapides animan-tium.Gemmis his annumerantur lapides, qui in animantiu corporibus e peculiari glutinoso femine generantur, quod pro-gressu ætatis, nativo colore concoctum & frigore constrictum coalescit.
Nobiliores sunt hi, qui in terrestri animali reperiuntur.
Chelidonius.Chelidonius, qui est lapillus exiguus in juvencularum Hirundinum ventriculo inventus, colore fusco, ex nigro aut subrufo permixto.
Alectorius.Alectorius est lapis Cristallo obscuro similis, in ventriculo Capi, anno ætatis 9. & s.[?] generatus, magnitudine fabæ.
Aetites.Aëtites est lapis cortice duro, scabro & minime levi, in Aquilæ nido inventus.
Borax.Borax alias Chelonites vel Bufonis est lapis in Bufonis senis[?] & magni reperto[?] capite.
Quadrus.Quadrus est lapis in cerebro Vulturis.

page.notes: Running head "CAPVT XIIII." and page number 199 are printed at the top; catchword "Sau-" and signature "N 4" are at the foot. Doubtful readings: "intern" followed by an abbreviation mark, read as internꝰ[?]; "& s." after "9." (possibly an abbreviation); "senis" after "Bufonis" and "reperto" at the end of the Borax paragraph are uncertain. Marginal notes carry small marks ("Magnes*"), but no matching reference marks are visible in the text. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout.
